Subject: Marketplace private offer — billing split / partner credit question

Sean —

Thanks for taking this. We're working on a Private Offer for a joint customer (Acme Logistics) and the conversation with our RevOps team surfaced a few open items we need to reconcile before legal signs:

- Marketplace list price vs. reseller net: how are credits/discounts surfaced on AWS/GCP catalog entries?
- Partner margin: our revops requires a minimum gross margin floor of ~22% on net revenue after cloud fees before we can resell. Can Redwood accommodate that via a partner credit or do you require upfront list price discounts?
- True-up mechanics: we prefer a monthly true-up (commit-based rebate) rather than retroactive credits if that makes implementation easier.

I've attached the current private offer terms from our side (current_po_terms.pdf). Can we do a quick sync early next week? Ideally include Ben from channel ops and someone from finance to confirm tax handling.

Tom —

Thanks for the context and the attachment. Quick read-through notes and a proposal for options so we can converge on what your RevOps needs:

1) Marketplace vs. reseller net presentation
   - On AWS Private Offers the purchaser sees the Catalog list price; the reseller net is handled off-catalog via the private offer price we set. For GCP Marketplace, list price constraints mean we typically need to set an "anchor" SKU and then apply a partner passback/credit off-invoice to preserve your margin.

2) Partner margin approaches (two viable methods)
   A) List-price uplift + reseller passback (upfront list price on marketplace, Redwood issues monthly partner credit back to CloudBroker).
   B) Commit-based rebate / true-up (we apply a smaller upfront discount on the PO and then rebate to you monthly based on commit attainment).

3) Tax and billing handling
   - We need to confirm whether CloudBroker will be the billed party on AWS (you take the invoice) or whether Acme will be billed and you receive a reseller payment. That affects VAT/sales tax flow. Please confirm.

4) Information we need from you before legal:
   - Expected monthly usage profile (tokens / embeddings / concurrency peak) — helps choose tiering and whether we can compress pricing into a SKU bucket.
   - Confirmation if 22% is the floor after Redwood's take or after cloud pass-throughs.

Attached a simple workbook (partner_pricing_workbook.xlsx) with two worked examples (Option A: passback, Option B: commit rebate). If you can populate the usage tab with projected monthly consumption for 12 months we can run the math and loop legal.

Proposed sync: Mon 31 Aug 10:00 PT — ok on your side?

Thanks — I cc'd Ben & Laura for channel ops/finance validation.

Regards,

Sean —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the workbook — filled the usage tab with a baseline and an upside scenario (link to folder below). A few clarifications from our side:

- The 22% margin requirement is a floor on our gross margin after Redwood's take and after cloud market fees (i.e., the net we remit to our P&L). If Redwood applied a partner credit monthly that would be easiest for us operationally.
- We can be the billed party on AWS (we have reseller status) which simplifies tax, but on GCP Marketplace the buyer-facing list price may still show the catalog price — so we need the passback to be actionable.
- Legal prefers a commit-based rebate (monthly true-up) keyed to committed spend. Is Redwood able to attach an automatic monthly credit to CloudBroker's billing account tied to a HubSpot deal or PO id?

Link to the populated workbook and supporting docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-cloudbroker-pricing

Legal note: We'll need an addendum that states clear escalation for missed true-ups and an audit window (90 days).

If you can send a short internal note on the two options you proposed (A vs B) and the systems work required for automated monthly credits, that will help our CFO sign off.

Thanks,
Tom

Team — forwarding Tom's replies and the workbook. Quick internal take and suggested next steps to put to RevOps/Legal/Finance:

Executive summary:
- Option A (passback): Redwood sets a slightly higher public list price on marketplace SKUs, then issues a monthly partner credit to CloudBroker to reach their 22% floor. Pros: minimal changes to checkout flow; works cleanly on AWS Private Offer. Cons: requires a monthly credit reconciliation and creates an accounts-payable touchpoint for Redwood.

- Option B (commit-based rebate / true-up): Redwood offers a committed discount structure (lower upfront price) with monthly true-up payments to CloudBroker if commit thresholds met. Pros: predictable for both parties; aligns incentives. Cons: requires integrating commit tracking and automating monthly rebate issuance; slightly more engineering/finance work to instrument.

Operational ask:
1) Engineer the monthly credit automation for the passback approach (small webhook + ledger entry) — estimate 1-2 sprints for a minimal viable flow tied to invoice ids.
2) Finance to confirm tax treatment if CloudBroker is billed vs. buyer-billed.
3) Legal to prepare a short addendum for the true-up audit window (90 days) and escalation.

Attached: proposal_option_A.pdf (draft language for passback credit)

Recommend we propose both options to CloudBroker and note an implementation timeline:
- Passback (fast): 3 weeks to implement automation + addendum signoff.
- Commit rebate (medium): 6-8 weeks to instrument commit tracking and automate rebates.

I'll set up a meeting with Finance and Eng leads to scope the automation if Sean agrees.

Ben
